source.title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Chang-Sheng Wang; Yihua Zhang; Jing-Han Jia; Parikshit Ram; Dennis Wei; Yuguang Yao; Soumyadeep Pal; Nathalie Baracaldo; Si-Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether downstream fine-tuning restores information after unlearning, not whether fine-tuning defeats safety alignment or refusal behavior. It does not test response-token KL, compliant prefixes, suffixes, decoding changes, or safety localization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own unlearning and post-unlearning fine-tuning results, which are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Its discussion of fine-tuning aligned models compromising safety is background citing other work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether downstream fine-tuning recovers knowledge removed by machine unlearning (WMDP forget quality, MUSE VerbMem/KnowMem). It does not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance in safety-aligned models, per-token KL, prefilling/suffix attacks, safety localization, or deepening of refusal. Qi et al. (2024) is cited only as background in Related Work. Unlearning robustness is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Existing unlearning methods (NPO, RMU) are vulnerable to downstream fine-tuning, even on unrelated tasks. ILU, an IRM-based regularizer using a single unrelated dataset, makes unlearning more resilient across unseen fine-tuning tasks while preserving fine-tuning accuracy. The authors suggest, without testing it, that this could extend to safety alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies unlearning methods (NPO and RMU) and adds invariance regularization, then evaluates whether downstream fine-tuning recovers forgotten information. It does not use the original safety-fine-tuning intervention or measure refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness varied with the invariance-regularization dataset and parameter λ. The paper reports that one unrelated fine-tuning set could outperform multiple sets or the forget set for its unlearning-robustness task.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign downstream fine-tuning on unrelated tasks (GSM8K, AGNews, etc.) restores WMDP knowledge removed by unlearning. RMU forget quality falls from 0.68 to about 0.42 and NPO from 0.52 to about 0.47 average RA. The original model's level is 0.36–0.37.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unrelated benign fine-tuning reverses machine unlearning of hazardous knowledge, analogous to benign fine-tuning eroding safety alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: A relearning attack on 60 forget-set instances for 1 epoch cuts RMU forget quality from 0.68 to 0.36 and NPO from 0.52 to 0.37. The ILU and SAM variants drop less.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small number of forget-set examples rapidly restores unlearned hazardous knowledge.

fits_no_version.finding: Invariance regularization with one unrelated dataset raises average post-fine-tuning robust accuracy: RMU from 0.42 to 0.65 and NPO from 0.47 to 0.56. On LLaMA3-8B-Instruct it matches TAR at 0.70.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Invariance regularization makes unlearning persistent under downstream fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: On MUSE-News, WinoGrande fine-tuning raises NPO VerbMem from 2.53 to 57.27 (original 58.40). ILU stays at 0.00.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream fine-tuning restores memorized content after unlearning, and invariance regularization prevents this.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The reported measures concern unlearning efficacy or memorization recovery, not user-directed harmful-request refusal. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the cited table results. The paper's experiments center mainly on one base model for WMDP, with additional settings for other benchmarks and a LLaMA3-8B-Instruct comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Many per-task values in Table 2 and the full per-condition MUSE-News and MUSE-Books results in Table A1 are not itemized. The catalog records aggregate Table 2 results, selected relearning-attack comparisons, the Table 4 aggregate, and the stated MUSE-News WinoGrande example; omitted values do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning effects on refusal or harmful compliance. The relearning attack recovers WMDP knowledge accuracy, not refusals.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance of safety-aligned models. Benign fine-tuning here restores unlearned knowledge, not compliance.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks. The task-vector cosine analysis concerns unlearning directions only.
Deepening refusal beyond first tokens. ILU is an unlearning-robustness regularizer, not refusal deepening.

record.verdict_notes: Relation is changed from discusses to cites_only: the original source Qi et al. is cited once as background. The 'harmful knowledge' here is WMDP multiple-choice accuracy, not refusal behaviour, so no row bears on any version. The authors' future-work remark about safety alignment is not a result.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful fine-tuning examples make safety-trained chat models comply with harmful requests or remove refusals.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data raises harmful compliance or reduces refusal in safety-trained chat models.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across harmful-prompt response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass safety behavior.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety behavior to be shallow.
Training to spread safety beyond initial response tokens and whether such safety persists.
